concepts.name: File-based routing with app directory
concepts.summary: Understand that folders under app define URL segments and that a page file makes a segment publicly reachable.

concepts.name: Page and layout files
concepts.summary: Explain how page files render route UI and layout files wrap pages and persist across navigation.

concepts.name: Server Components by default
concepts.summary: Understand that components in the App Router render on the server by default and send no component JavaScript to the client.

concepts.name: Client Components and use client
concepts.summary: Recognise when the use client directive is needed, such as for state, effects and event handlers.

concepts.name: Navigation with next/link
concepts.summary: Use the Link component to navigate between routes without a full page reload.

concepts.name: Dynamic route segments
concepts.summary: Understand that a folder named in square brackets captures a URL part as a parameter.

concepts.name: Optimised images with next/image
concepts.summary: Remember that the Image component resizes, lazy-loads and serves modern formats and requires dimensions or fill to avoid layout shift.

misconceptions.text: Next.js is a separate language or replacement for React rather than a framework built on top of it.
Any file inside the app folder automatically becomes a route.
Every component needs use client to be interactive or to work at all.

concepts.name: Reading dynamic route params
concepts.summary: Access path params and search params in pages and use them to load the right data.

concepts.name: Async data fetching in server components
concepts.summary: Write async server components that await fetch calls or database queries directly.

concepts.name: Nested layouts and route groups
concepts.summary: Compose nested layouts and use route groups to organise routes or split layouts without changing URLs.

concepts.name: Loading and error UI files
concepts.summary: Apply special files to show loading states, handle errors and render not-found pages per segment.

concepts.name: Passing server data to client components
concepts.summary: Pass serialisable props from server to client components and compose them using children.

concepts.name: Metadata API
concepts.summary: Set static and dynamic page titles and descriptions using metadata exports.

concepts.name: Programmatic navigation hooks
concepts.summary: Use navigation hooks in client components and redirect in server code to change routes.

misconceptions.text: You must use useEffect to fetch data in the App Router.
Route groups in parentheses add a segment to the URL.
Any value, including functions, can be passed as props from a server to a client component.

concepts.name: Rendering strategies SSG SSR ISR
concepts.summary: Analyse a route's data needs to choose between static, dynamic and revalidated rendering.

concepts.name: Fetch caching and revalidation
concepts.summary: Control cache behaviour of data fetches with time-based and on-demand revalidation and reason about staleness.

concepts.name: Server Actions for mutations
concepts.summary: Implement mutations and form handling with server actions, including validation and revalidating affected data.

concepts.name: Route handlers
concepts.summary: Build HTTP endpoints with route files exporting method handlers and decide when they are preferable to server actions.

concepts.name: Streaming with Suspense
concepts.summary: Split slow data into Suspense boundaries so the page streams progressively.

concepts.name: Pages Router data functions
concepts.summary: Compare getServerSideProps and getStaticProps in the Pages Router with App Router equivalents to read and migrate legacy code.

concepts.name: Static params generation
concepts.summary: Prerender dynamic routes at build time and control behaviour for unlisted params.

concepts.name: Environment variables and exposure
concepts.summary: Keep secrets server-only and expose only NEXT_PUBLIC variables to the browser bundle.

misconceptions.text: getServerSideProps works inside app directory pages.
Server actions are only a convenience and do not create public endpoints needing authorisation checks.
ISR re-renders the page on every request so content is always fresh.

concepts.name: Middleware request interception
concepts.summary: Use middleware matchers to redirect, rewrite or modify headers and judge what belongs there versus in route code.

concepts.name: Authentication and authorisation placement
concepts.summary: Evaluate where to verify sessions so that data access is protected at the data layer rather than only in layouts or middleware.

concepts.name: Caching layers interplay
concepts.summary: Diagnose stale or unexpectedly dynamic output by tracing request memoisation, data cache, full route cache and client router cache.

concepts.name: Server and client boundary design
concepts.summary: Evaluate where to place client boundaries to minimise bundle size while preserving interactivity.

concepts.name: Performance optimisation
concepts.summary: Assess and improve LCP, CLS and INP using image, font and script optimisation and code splitting.

concepts.name: Runtimes Node and Edge
concepts.summary: Analyse the constraints of Edge versus Node runtimes for each route and choose accordingly.

concepts.name: Parallel and intercepting routes
concepts.summary: Model advanced UI patterns such as modals and dashboards using parallel slots and intercepting routes.

concepts.name: Vercel deployment and previews
concepts.summary: Analyse how a Next.js app maps onto Vercel serverless functions, static assets, preview deployments and environment scopes.

misconceptions.text: Checking authentication in a layout is enough to protect all data beneath it.
Middleware can run any Node API and is the right place for heavy logic like database queries.
Putting use client at the top of a page is harmless for performance.

concepts.name: Rendering architecture trade-offs
concepts.summary: Judge static, dynamic and partially prerendered designs for a product by cost, freshness, latency and complexity.

concepts.name: Cache strategy design
concepts.summary: Design tag and path invalidation schemes across data sources, CDN and client so freshness guarantees are explicit.

concepts.name: Self-hosting and portability
concepts.summary: Evaluate running Next.js outside Vercel, including standalone output, shared caches across instances and platform feature gaps.

concepts.name: Monorepo and large-app structure
concepts.summary: Design project structure, shared packages and build pipelines that scale across teams.

concepts.name: Observability and failure handling
concepts.summary: Evaluate instrumentation, tracing and error boundaries to detect and diagnose production issues in server and client code.

concepts.name: Security hardening
concepts.summary: Assess threats such as data leakage across the server-client boundary, CSRF on actions and missing headers, and apply mitigations.

concepts.name: Migration strategy Pages to App
concepts.summary: Plan an incremental migration from Pages Router to App Router with coexistence, risk control and verification.

misconceptions.text: Next.js apps only run well on Vercel and cannot be self-hosted with full features.
Maximising static generation is always the best architecture regardless of data freshness needs.
A migration to the App Router must be done all at once because the two routers cannot coexist.
